items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the not-for-profit corporation law, in relation to leasing
cemetery lands
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6257

SPONSOR: COMRIE
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the not-for-profit corporation law, in relation to leas-
ing cemetery lands

 
PURPOSE:

The bill addresses general procedures when a regulated New York cemetery
desires to lease a portion of cemetery property not currently needed for
burial purposes. The leasing of surplus cemetery land has been permitted
in New York for many years. However, there is no standardized statutory
process for applications to the state cemetery board for such temporary
leases. This bill standardizes the review process and requirements for
such an application and for returning the land to burial space at the
conclusion of the lease.

This continuation of existing leases and the standardization of applica-
tions to permit additional lease opportunities will provide needed
revenue to prevent cemetery abandonment. It will also build long-term
statutory permanent maintenance funds for the preservation of these
non-profit entities.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill provides findings and declarations related to the
need for continuing the leasing of cemetery lands to use the income for
the maintenance and preservation of the cemetery and to protect the
public interest.

Section 2 would add a new section 1506-e of the not-for-profit corpo-
ration law to add several provisions related to an application and
approval for a leasing of surplus land not currently needed by the ceme-
tery for burial purposes.

This section requires all such leases be approved by the state cemetery
board, composed of the designees of the secretary of state, attorney
general and commissioner of health, unless they involve a lease or
license to grow and harvest crops with a term less than five years; a
lease of the dwelling of the caretaker or employee of the cemetery; or
the renewal or assignment of an existing lease that was approved by the
cemetery board or a court, that does not change the scope of the exist-
ing lease.

Additional provisions include posting requirements for notification of
the public and lot owners, compliance with related party transaction
restrictions, lease terms, bonding, screening of the leased property,
the payment of taxes, the removal of any structures or infrastructure
not being retained by the cemetery at the conclusion of the lease, and
provisions for requiring proceeds of the leases to be directed to the
cemetery's permanent maintenance fund or a portion of which may be
approved by the cemetery board for specific projects to maintain and
preserve or expand current cemetery operations.

Section 3 provides that any previous leases, including any right of
renewal under such agreements that were previously approved by the state
cemetery board, shall not be impacted by this new process.
Section 4 states that this bill shall take effect immediately.

 
EXISTING LAW:

State regulated non-profit cemeteries have been leasing surplus land for
many years utilizing the cemetery board's regulatory process for major
renovations and various broad statutory provisions.  There is currently
no standardized process for review and approval of such leases. This
bill would standardize the process and create clear legislative authori-
ty for such agreements.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

While the leasing of surplus cemetery land has been permitted in New
York for many years, there is no standardized statutory process for
applications to the state cemetery board for such temporary leases.  The
state has a vital interest in the public service that public cemeteries
provide and in their viability as not-for-profit entities.  Many ceme-
teries face falling demand for traditional burial services and other
financial pressures. It is therefore necessary for the state to provide
greater flexibility for cemeteries to generate income to prevent their
operational failure and abandonment to local governments and impacts on
the state fiscal plan.

This bill would simultaneously protect the interests of cemetery lot
owners, visitors and the financial impacts on local governments. It is
in the public interest that cemeteries with surplus land are able to
receive income from such land for a period of time without altering the
purpose of public cemeteries or negatively impacting the operation of
the cemetery and the use of cemetery land.

The additional benefit of this legislation is that it not only provides
revenue for the preservation of non-profit cemetery operations, in some
instances, it would also place surplus land on the tax rolls.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state. In some instances, positive property tax implications
for local governments.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

tructure not being retained by the cemetery at the conclusion of the

Section 3. Provides that any previous leases, including any right of
renewal under such agreements that were previously approved by the state
cemetery board, shall not be impacted by this new process.

Section 4. The effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

State regulated non-profit cemeteries have been leasing surplus land for
many years utilizing the cemetery board's regulatory process for major
renovations and various broad statutory provisions. There is currently
no standardized statutory process for application, review and approval
of such leases. This bill would standardize the process and create clear
legislative authority for such agreements.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.
 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
